extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures. Unlike existing benchmarks, MMMU focuses on advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MMMU dataset was meticulously curated through a three-stage process. First, common university majors were reviewed to select subjects where visual inputs are commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concerns of foundation models, the annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks. This process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources. The detailed annotation protocol is in Appendix A.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset sources include college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and licensing regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The questions were selected to avoid immediate answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process was conducted over several months, with the final dataset compiled by June 2024.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data underwent three stages of quality control: 1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by the authors to eliminate any duplications. 2) The problems were distributed among different co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format. 3) The authors categorized the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with the design criteria due to their simplistic nature, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation protocol involved recruiting over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The detailed annotation protocol is in Appendix A.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotation process utilized a user-friendly web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification, which significantly improved the workflow for data curation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process included rigorous quality control steps such as lexical overlap and source URL similarity checks to identify potential duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and categorization into difficulty levels. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset includes 11.5K questions, with an average of 1.03 images per question. The questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators were over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors. They were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and avoid data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released under the MIT License and is maintained by the authors. The dataset is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/. The authors plan to update the dataset periodically to include more questions and improve the quality of the existing ones.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models (LMMs) can achieve by assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains. It provides a comprehensive benchmark that aligns with the expectations of skilled adults in these fields, potentially stimulating the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases due to the manual curation process and the focus on college-level subjects. The authors caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The authors argue that strong performance on this benchmark should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system. The challenging nature of MMMU is evident from the performance of over 30 models and human experts. To strike a balance between complexity and practicality, MMMU combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions, enabling the assessment of diverse subjects while addressing the challenges associated with evaluating open-ended responses.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating the capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs) in the context of Expert AGI. It can be used for training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning of models. The dataset is particularly useful for assessing advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.
